hints: Focus on the type of decomposition each Group 2 carbonate and each Group 2 nitrate undergoes when heated strongly.
Remember carbonates give a metal oxide plus $\text{CO}_2$, while nitrates give a metal oxide plus $\text{NO}_2$ plus $\text{O}_2$.
List all the products from the four reactions, then cross out repeats because $\text{CaO}$, $\text{CO}_2$, $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ appear more than once.
walkthrough:
**Recall carbonate decomposition**

Both calcium carbonate and strontium carbonate break down in the same way to give the metal oxide and carbon dioxide.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{MCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MO} + \text{CO}_2$$
So we get $\text{CaO} + \text{CO}_2$ from one, and $\text{SrO} + \text{CO}_2$ from the other.

**Recall nitrate decomposition**

Both calcium nitrate and strontium nitrate break down in the same way to give the metal oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen.

Chemical equation:
$$2\text{M}(\text{NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$
So we get $\text{CaO} + \text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$ from one, and $\text{SrO} + \text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$ from the other.

**Count only different products**

Now collect everything together and count each unique substance only once.

Unique list:
$$\text{CaO}, \text{SrO}, \text{CO}_2, \text{NO}_2, \text{O}_2$$
That is 3 solids and gases combined into 5 different products in total.

options.A: 4 is too few. It often comes from thinking there is one product per starting material, or from forgetting that nitrate decomposition gives two different gases, $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$, not just one.
options.B: 5 is correct. The distinct products are $\text{CaO}$, $\text{SrO}$, $\text{CO}_2$, $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$. $\text{CO}_2$ is common to both carbonates, $\text{CaO}$ is common to calcium carbonate and calcium nitrate, $\text{SrO}$ is common to strontium carbonate and strontium nitrate, and $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ are common to both nitrates.
options.C: 7 is too many. It comes from only partly cancelling duplicates, for example counting $\text{CaO}$ or $\text{SrO}$ twice when they are formed from both the carbonate and the nitrate of the same metal.
options.D: 8 is the total if you simply add up products without cancelling any repeats. It treats $\text{CaO}$, $\text{SrO}$, $\text{CO}_2$, $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ as new every time, but the question asks for different products.
